title: Graphing a Piecewise Reciprocal and Linear Function
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Analyze and describe the graph of the piecewise-defined function G(x) = 1/x for x < 0, and G(x) = x for x >= 0.
finalAnswer: \text{Third-quadrant hyperbola branch } y = 1/x \text{ for } x < 0, \text{ and first-quadrant ray } y = x \text{ for } x \ge 0

steps.title: Analyze the Negative Branch (x < 0)
steps.explanation: For x < 0, the graph is the third-quadrant branch of the hyperbola y = 1/x passing through (-1, -1), approaching 0^- as x -> -infinity and plunging toward -infinity as x -> 0^-.
steps.why: On (-inf, 0), the reciprocal 1/x is strictly negative and has asymptotes y = 0 and x = 0.

steps.title: Analyze the Non-Negative Branch (x >= 0)
steps.explanation: For x >= 0, the graph is the ray y = x starting at the closed point (0, 0) and rising with slope 1 through (1, 1) in the first quadrant.
steps.why: The second rule applies at x = 0, placing a solid point at the origin (0, 0).

steps.title: State the Domain and Range
steps.explanation: The negative branch covers all negative outputs (-inf, 0), while the non-negative branch covers [0, inf), so the overall range is (-inf, inf) with an infinite discontinuity at x = 0.
steps.why: The union of (-inf, 0) and [0, inf) is the entire real line (-inf, inf).
